claims.content: To extract the contents of a selected archive.

scope_contract.goal_statement: To extract the contents of a selected archive.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The User extracts the contents of a selected archive into a folder.
scope_contract.start_boundary: A compressed archive has been selected by the User.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The selected archive's contents are extracted into a folder.

excluded_adjacent_actions: Using the extracted files after extraction
variant_dimensions: Whether all archive content or selected content is extracted

claims.content: User
A compressed archive has been selected by the User.
The User selects the 'Extraction Interface' (the 'Extract' dialog window).
The User chooses the storage space (output folder) in the Extraction Interface where the extracted files will be saved.
The User specifies the output name and selects how to handle an existing homonym file or archive in the selected storage space.
The User configures extraction options in the Extraction Interface, including 'Extract in new folder' and format options such as 'Extract' mode and 'Auto rename extracted files'.
If the selected archive is encrypted, the system requires the User to enter the password (and keyfile if applicable) in the Extraction Interface to access the contents.
The User clicks the 'Ok' button at the bottom right of the dialog to finalize the extraction operation.

The system extracts the selected archive's contents into the chosen output folder and displays an 'Extracting:' progress list showing columns for Name, Type, Size (B), Packed, Date/time, Attributes, CRC, and Full name.
Upon completion, the system displays summary statistics ('0 dir(s), 0 file(s), 0 B') and presents 'Ok' and 'Cancel' buttons for user confirmation or abort.

Diverges from main-flow Step 1: Instead of choosing an existing output folder as the storage space, the User selects the 'Extract in new folder' checkbox (or uses the 'Extract to new folder' function) in the Extraction Interface; the system extracts the archive contents into a newly created folder.

Diverges from main-flow Step 2: Instead of manually specifying how to handle a homonym file or archive, the User configures the 'Auto rename extracted files' format option via the Extraction Interface dropdown, causing filename conflicts to be handled by automatic renaming.

Diverges from main-flow Step 3: Instead of configuring the 'extract to new folder' option through the Extraction Interface controls, the User presses Shift+N in the extraction layout to toggle the 'extract to new folder' option on or off.

Diverges from main-flow Step 6: If the User has initiated extraction while browsing within the archive and has selected specific objects, the system extracts only those selected objects rather than the entire archive content.

claims.content: The selected archive's contents are extracted into the user-chosen storage space (folder) in non-compressed format.

The archive whose contents are extracted is preserved: it is neither destroyed nor deleted and is not left empty; it retains its content and name and remains saved at the same place in the computer system where it was initially stored.
Upon completion, the Extraction Interface displays summary statistics in the format 'X dir(s), Y file(s), Z B' at the bottom left.
After successful extraction, the Extraction Interface presents 'Ok' and 'Cancel' buttons, allowing the User to confirm/close or abort/exit without further action.

(atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (No cited source content explicitly supports 'successful completion' or placement in an 'extraction completion dialog'.))

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 2 says only that 'In case of error, the application provides users with appropriate help messages.' It does not specify whether extraction aborts, returns to a Main Flow step, terminates, or enters an explicit terminal failure/prevention state, so the branch lacks a clear outcome.

inconsistency_hints: Main-flow step 7 presents 'Ok' and 'Cancel' buttons after completion, but this postcondition claims the system presents 'Explore' and 'Ok'; the Explore control is not reached and the stated button set contradicts the main flow.

The main flow's completion step (step 7) only reaches a summary of '0 dir(s), 0 file(s), 0 B' with Ok/Cancel buttons. It does not establish the postcondition's 'Job successfully completed' message with input size, output size, compression percentage, and processing time, so that postcondition is not reachable as written.
